title: POC weekly sync - session affinity & prompt reuse
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on caching effectiveness and prompt reuse strategy. Team reviewed KV/prefix hit-rate trends after canonicalization, discussed session-affinity approach to boost warm cache utilization, and debated TTL/eviction policy for high-cardinality prompts. Action items include running a 24-hour prefetch experiment, adding canonicalization rules for 6 additional templates, and a short benchmark to quantify cost savings. Agreed to reconvene next Tuesday for results and to share updated eviction policy docs.
topics: KV cache hit-rate trend (week over week)
eviction TTL and LRU vs TTL+LFU hybrid
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-19 15:30 PT | Duration 42 min | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Maya (Echelon), Derrick (Echelon CTO), Priya (Echelon SRE), Arjun (NLP)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. Quick agenda: hit rates, session affinity idea, canonicalization progress from Arjun, then next steps. Can everyone hear okay?
[00:05] Maya: Yeah, loud and clear.
[00:10] Derrick: Yep.

[02:12] Lena: I'll pull up the dashboard — so last week we were at roughly 18% KV hit across user-facing templates. After the first round of canonicalization we spiked to 34% Friday night, then dropped to 28% during peak. That's the smoothing effect of new user sessions, so we're looking at both steady gains and volatility.

[03:01] Arjun: Quick note — the spike happened because we unified date formats and stripped trailing punctuation on the 6 biggest templates.

[03:45] Priya: Is the 28% number measured on production sampling or staging? We need to make sure metric windows are aligned.
[04:01] Lena: Production 2% sampling, but the dashboard extrapolates to full traffic; we logged raw counts as well. There's noise during our nightly batch jobs.

[06:05] Samir: Okay, cool. Two things I want to call out — first, session affinity might help: if we route a user's requests to the same serving worker (or pool) for a short affinity window, their KV cache will warm locally and the apparent hit rate for that user goes up without changing global cache size. Second, canonicalization for prompts is low-hanging fruit.

[07:02] Derrick: My concern with affinity is sticky routing increases tail risk if that worker is overloaded, and it complicates autoscaling. How do we mitigate?
[07:16] Lena: Good point. We recommend an affinity policy that's soft — 10 to 30 second affinity with fallback to stateless routing if SLA or CPU exceeds threshold. That keeps warm caches but allows failover.

[08:00] Maya: Can you quantify the expected latency improvement per user session? We need numbers to sell this internally.
[08:18] Lena: Based on our small tests, warm-cache requests are ~45 to 60 ms faster on avg for these templates. End-to-end we saw p50 p50 absolute drop of 60 ms and p95 drop of about 120 ms when affinity + canonicalization combined.

[09:30] Arjun: I want to emphasize template deduping — we added canonical forms for the 6 dev templates, but there are another 14 templates with minor variants (capitalization, trailing context) that would probably double hit-rate if canonicalized.

[10:42] Samir: Let's dig into eviction. Current default is LRU with a 5k-entry cap per worker and TTL of 1 hour. The ask from Echelon was to bias towards recency for interactive workflows but also retain some moderately-frequent keys longer. We suggested TTL+LFU hybrid.
[11:12] Priya: Hybrid sounds reasonable but it's operationally more complex. Do we have telemetry to show which keys would benefit from LFU?
[11:30] Lena: Yes, we can export per-key frequency histograms for a 48-hour window — we've got a script that produces the tail distribution. I'll share the report.

[13:00] Derrick: Can we avoid blowing up memory footprint? If we keep more hot keys, we may need to resize the pool.
[13:10] Samir: Right — tradeoff is memory vs token cost. We estimated that increasing effective hit-rate from 28% to 45% reduces token generation by ~18% on average; for your workload that maps to approx $0.55 per 1M tokens saved at current rates. It's a rough ballpark.

[15:00] Arjun: Quick question about prefetch heuristics — can we prefetch next-turn tokens when we see conversational intent? For example, when user asks a sequence of related steps, prefetch can reduce cold-starts.
[15:20] Lena: We support request prefetching at the router level as an opt-in policy. It adds a little CPU overhead but can bump effective hit-rate by 3-7% in sequential flows.

[16:30] Maya: Could prefetch cause wasted tokens if the user abandons the flow? We worry about cost.
[16:38] Lena: Yes — that's why heuristics use probability thresholds and don't prefetch for low-confidence scenarios. Also you can bound prefetch depth to 1 next-turn only.

[18:10] Samir: On canonicalization rules, Arjun said he pushed a patch to the shared repo with 6 rules. Could you summarize the rules and the expected additional coverage?
[18:25] Arjun: Sure — normalize dates to YYYY-MM-DD, strip salutations, collapse repeated whitespace, remove trailing punctuation, map synonyms for key verbs (e.g., "book" -> "schedule"), and remove user IDs from prompts when not needed. That covers about 42% of low-cardinality variants.

[20:00] Priya: Any concerns about losing signal by removing user IDs? Some prompts include user-specific context for personalization.
[20:12] Arjun: We only strip IDs in the canonicalization pass for the cache key; the full prompt is still available to the model. It's just a normalization layer for cache key computation.

[22:00] Lena: We also noticed a weird artefact: some clients are sending a session token in the middle of the prompt which produces unique keys. We recommended moving session tokens to metadata headers rather than embedding in prompt text. Priya, can you check ingesters?
[22:22] Priya: Yup, we'll audit the client side this week.

[24:00] Samir: Metrics to track: global KV hit-rate, per-template hit-rate, per-user warm-hit ratio, average latency delta for warm vs cold, memory utilization, and token-savings estimate. Lena, can you add these to the dashboard and share the query?
[24:20] Lena: On it; I'll include the raw count logs and annotation for canonicalization rollouts.

[26:00] Maya: We want a short cost forecast for the board. Can you produce a two-scenario forecast: conservative (no affinity, only canonicalization) and optimistic (affinity + canonicalization + prefetch)?
[26:20] Samir: Absolutely. We'll run a 72-hour simulated trace on your sampled traffic to produce both scenarios.

[28:00] Derrick: Regarding autoscaling concerns — if we use soft affinity, do we need to modify the autoscaler to be affinity-aware?
[28:12] Lena: Not necessarily — the router respects autoscaler thresholds and will avoid placing new affinity binds when CPU > 70% on target pool. The only change is the router maintains a short affinity map; that has tiny memory cost.

[30:15] Arjun: One more data point: in the staging prefetch run we saw an increase in CPU by ~6% and a hit-rate bump of 4.2%. This suggests prefetch is net positive for sequential journeys.

[31:40] Priya: OK that helps. For eviction policy test, can you propose concrete params to A/B? Like LRU baseline, LFU-weighted TTL=2h, and hybrid LRU+LFU with 10s affinity window.
[31:55] Samir: Yes, we can run three cohorts. We'll need to tag users for cohorts in the router and track per-cohort metrics.

[33:00] Maya: Timeline — we want to show early results by Friday. Is that doable?
[33:08] Lena: If Echelon can flip canonicalization rules and deploy the router affinity flag by tomorrow morning, we can start a 48-hour run and have preliminary numbers by Friday.

[34:20] Priya: We'll prioritize the client-side cleanup and canonicalization merges today.

[35:10] Samir: Great. A couple of operational items — we'll attach the eviction policy doc and a short runbook for rollback if affinity causes load spikes. Also we'll include a short notebook to simulate token cost impact.

[36:30] Arjun: Small thing — some of our logs show mis-escaped unicode from mobile clients which creates unique keys. We should canonicalize unicode normalization too.
[36:45] Lena: Good catch. Add that to the rule list.

[38:00] Samir: Let's do a recap and next steps.
[38:05] Samir: Recap: canonicalization pushed for 6 templates; expand to 14 more. Run cohorts: baseline LRU, LFU-TTL, hybrid with soft affinity 10s. Start 48-hour prefetch test with depth=1 and probability threshold 0.7. Dashboard updates and cost forecast by Friday. Client audit on session tokens and unicode done today.

[40:00] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[40:05] Derrick: Thank you.

[41:30] Samir: We'll follow up with a calendar invite for next Tuesday and attach the docs. Bye.
